subject: Post-call: controls gap summary + certification playbook proposal
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@helixcare.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: controls gap + next steps

Alex — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Current posture: internal security team has started SOC 2 Type I work (controls defined, documentation in progress). No formal Type II report yet.
- Data/regulatory: some product flows touch PHI; you indicated need to confirm HIPAA boundary for the Helix analytics pipeline. GDPR data residency concerns for EU customers were flagged but not scoped.
- Procurement ask: you will run two vendor checks in parallel — technical RFI and legal T&Cs review.

Immediate asks from Redwood
1) Please complete the attached vendor security questionnaire (HelixCare_RFI_answers_v1.pdf) — fills the items we discussed (controls owner, encryption at rest/in-transit, retention).
2) Confirm HIPAA boundary owners and any existing BAAs we should reference (Tom or Alex).
3) Share your preferred 90-day timeline for certification priorities: (a) prioritize SOC 2 Type II readiness or (b) ISO 27001 mapping first — either works, we’ll align the roadmap.

Proposed next steps (my suggested timeline)
- Week 0 (this week): Helix returns RFI answers and inventory doc.
- Week 1: 60-min controls scoping call (technical) with Laura + Priyom to map Redwood control expectations to Helix systems.
- Week 2–4: Redwood sends draft compliance playbook (controls mapping + incremental milestones) — see draft spreadsheet we’ll circulate.
- 30/60/90 day checkpoints to align on SOC scope, ISO baseline, and FedRAMP feasibility.

Attached: small stubbed RFI to speed answers. I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the controls scoping call — can you confirm availability for next Tue/Wed afternoon PT?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: controls gap + next steps

Alex — adding a couple technical notes ahead of the controls scoping call. Thanks for the overview today.

Quick notes from a controls perspective:
- SOC 2 scope: we’ll want to confirm the set of services/endpoints that will be in-scope for HelixCare’s SOC reporting. Typical options: API ingress, data storage, analytics jobs. Narrowing this now avoids rework later.
- HIPAA: if the analytics pipeline stores PHI, we treat datastore encryption, access logging, and BAA boundaries as mandatory controls for SOC scope.
- ISO 27001: mapping can run in parallel — initial gap list (Annex A mapping) can be produced from the RFI answers.

Pre-call checklist for your team (to prepare for the technical scoping):
- IAM diagram (high level) or list of identity providers
- Data flow for any PHI/PII data stores and retention windows
- Current endpoint inventory (S3 buckets, DB clusters, third-party integrations)

Priyom — I’ll need you on the scoping call to walk through encryption and logging expectations and to note any quick wins (e.g., enabling key rotation, centralized audit logging).

Happy to join next Tue/Wed — I’ll let Soojin pick a slot once we have preferences from Helix.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Security Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@helixcare.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Riley <triley@helixcare.com>, procurement@helixcare.com
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 09:41:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: controls gap + next steps

Soojin/Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and context from our side: 

RFI
- We’ll fill out the RFI by EOD Mon (08/09). Most items are straightforward; we will attach an inventory export.

SOC/GRC status
- SOC 2: control set defined, policies drafted; target to complete Type II readiness activities over the next 4–5 months. No Type II report yet.
- ISO 27001: leadership is open to pursuing, but budget cycle for certification is Q1 2027; we’re more focused on SOC 2 in the near term.
- FedRAMP: not on current roadmap — very long runway, requires significant platform changes. Happy to capture as long-term objective.

HIPAA/GDPR
- PHI boundary: our analytics pipeline stores derived clinical metrics; we’ll confirm with Tom whether this requires BAAs or anonymization first.
- GDPR: we have EU customers; data residency requests are ad-hoc so far.

Procurement
- Procurement will run parallel contract review — I’ve looped them in. They will expect an SOC attestation and our standard data processing addendum.

Availability
- Controls scoping call: Tue 08/11 11:00–12:00 PT or Wed 08/12 13:00–14:00 PT both work for our team. Please send an invite for the confirmed slot.

Thanks,
Alex Barnes
Director of Platform Engineering, HelixCare
alex.barnes@helixcare.com | +1 617-555-0103
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Controls scoping confirmed + draft playbook (attached)

Alex — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. I’ve booked Tue 11 Aug, 11:00–12:00 PT for the controls scoping call (calendar invite sent).

Attached is a short draft playbook (redwood-compliance-roadmap-draft.xlsx) that stitches together the next 90 days based on our conversation: 
- Phase 0 (days 0–7): RFI + inventory (Helix to return)
- Phase 1 (week 1–4): technical controls scoping (this call) + gap list from Laura/Priyom
- Phase 2 (month 1–3): prioritized hardening (IAM, encryption, logging), policy runbook, test evidence collection for SOC Type II readiness
- Phase 3 (month 3–6): external auditor readiness and pre-audit checklist; parallel ISO mapping if leadership confirms budget

Action items assigned
- Helix: return RFI and inventory by EOD Mon 08/09 (Alex / Tom).
- Redwood: produce initial gap list + recommended remediations within 5 business days after the scoping call (Laura/Priyom).
- Procurement: please confirm contract timelines and any mandatory vendor security questions to include in the RFI (cc’d).

A couple of notes on trade-offs we discussed: prioritizing SOC Type II readiness will get procurement the attestation they need faster; ISO/FedRAMP are heavier investments and we’ll treat them as follow-on tracks once SOC boundaries are stable.

I’ve included the prior messages below for context. Looking forward to the scoping call.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
